Answer: A
Reason: Broncholithiasis is characterized by a calcified lymph node eroding into or obstructing a bronchus, which leads to distal airway obstruction and subsequent segmental atelectasis (visible as consolidation/collapse in the left lower lobe on the lung window image). The combination of a calcified focus with associated atelectasis in a symptomatic patient (hemoptysis) strongly supports this diagnosis over a simple granuloma or malignancy.
